text: Same as MSPDI Project.
Same as MSPDI Project/UID. Before saving over a file, GRS checks this value, project.name and the file name to tell whether the file holds the same document.

Same as MSPDI Project/CalendarUID. GRS counts all working days with this one calendar. If it is absent or names no calendar, GRS uses the calendar with isBaseCalendar true and the smallest ordinal, else a built-in default.
Same as MSPDI Project/Name. GRS does not show it (the name shown on screen is title). It is used only to tell whether a file about to be overwritten is the same document.
Same as MSPDI Project/Title. GRS shows it at the top of the page and uses it as the default name of an exported file. When absent, the browser tab shows Untitled.
Same as MSPDI Project/Subject.
Same as MSPDI Project/Category.
Same as MSPDI Project/Company.
Same as MSPDI Project/Manager.
Same as MSPDI Project/Author. It is not who wrote the document last (documentStamp.lastEditedBy).
Same as MSPDI Project/Revision. It is not one of the documentStamp times.
Same as MSPDI Project/CreationDate. GRS writes it when it makes a new document.
Same as MSPDI Project/StartDate.
Same as MSPDI Project/StatusDate. GRS draws the status line on its day. Absent means no status line, and Delay Diagnostics does not run.
The fixed UTC offset of the clock that the schedule date-times are written in, for example UTC+09:00. It is standard time: daylight saving is never applied. GRS does not write it to MSPDI.

Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerDay: the length of one working day (1d) in minutes, {{S-128}} when absent. GRS warns when the document is opened if the working times of any working day add up to a total other than this value.
Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerWeek.
Same as MSPDI Project/DaysPerMonth.
Same as MSPDI Project/WeekStartDay, where 0 is Sunday. Absent means Monday (1).

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultStartTime: the time of day GRS gives a start that is set by the day (the start of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualStart, resume, project.startDate); {{S-482}} when absent. A milestone's start gets defaultFinishTime instead.

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultFinishTime: the time of day GRS gives a finish that is set by the day (the finish of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualFinish, stop, deadline, project.statusDate); {{S-483}} when absent. A milestone's start gets this time as well.
The hue of the theme, in degrees. Every color written as {"kind":"theme"} uses it. A new document starts with 214.

How many working days the progress point of a parent task may lie outside the progress points of the work below it, before Delay Diagnostics asks whether an update is missing. A new document starts with 1.
One counter for the uids of tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. Uids are never reused, so a new uid is always above this value.
How many times a file has been imported into this document; 0 means never. TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportNumber is compared with it.
The OutlineLevel at which the tasks of an imported file start (the project summary task is not counted); export writes from this number. A new document starts with 1.
The format the document came from: grs for a document made in GRS, pj12 or pj15 for an MSPDI file (pj15 when it has any element that only pj15 has). It is not written to MSPDI.

Carried MSPDI elements under this one, each written back in its place.
Same as MSPDI Calendar.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/UID.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/BaseCalendarUID: the calendar this one inherits from. GRS keeps the value but does not inherit: it counts only the days this calendar itself lists.
The order of the calendar as it came in the file, used to write the calendars back in that order.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/Name.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/IsBaseCalendar. Absent reads as false.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/WeekDays.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/Exceptions.

Carried MSPDI elements under this one, each written back in its place.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay.
The order of this weekday within its calendar, as it came in the file.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/DayType, where 1 is Sunday, except that 0 is not used: exception days are held in Exception.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/DayWorking. Absent reads as not working.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/WorkingTimes. Absent on a working day means the default spans {{S-580}}.

Carried MSPDI elements under this one, each written back in its place.
Same as MSPDI Exception.
The order of this exception within its calendar, as it came in the file.
Same as MSPDI Exception/Name.
Same as MSPDI Exception/TimePeriod/FromDate: the first day of the exception. GRS reads only the date and writes T00:00:00.
Same as MSPDI Exception/TimePeriod/ToDate: the last day of the exception, included. GRS reads only the date and writes T23:59:00.
Same as MSPDI Exception/DayWorking. Absent reads as not working.

Same as MSPDI Exception/Type. GRS counts only a one-off exception: recurrenceKind is 9 or absent, or is 1 and recurrencePeriod is absent or 1; it keeps the others unchanged without counting them. Write 1 for an exception you add.

type: int >=1, optional; when the property is absent: the file had no Period
text: Same as MSPDI Exception/Period.
Same as MSPDI Exception/WorkingTimes. Absent on a working day means the default spans {{S-580}}.

type: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional; when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: Carried MSPDI values of this element, under their MSPDI names.
Carried MSPDI elements under this one, each written back in its place.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime. GRS refuses spans of one day that overlap or do not start before they end; spans that only touch, such as one ending at 12:00 and one starting at 12:00, are fine.
The order of this span within its day; GRS writes the spans in the order of their start.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime/FromTime.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime/ToTime. 00:00:00 means 24:00, the end of the day.

Same as MSPDI Task. GRS reads the progress state with these checks, first match wins: no actualStart, not started; actualFinish set, finished; resumeValid false, suspended with no resume date; resume set, suspended with a resume date; otherwise in progress.
Same as MSPDI Task/UID.

type: int 0..2147483647, optional; when the property is absent: top of the WBS
text: The parent task in the WBS. Absent means a top-level task.
Same as MSPDI Task/CalendarUID, the calendar of this task alone. GRS keeps the value and writes it back, but counts working days with project.calendarUid only.
The order of this task among the tasks under the same parent task.
Same as MSPDI Task/Name.
Same as MSPDI Task/Notes.
Same as MSPDI Task/Start. GRS does not open a file in which a task has no start.
Same as MSPDI Task/Finish. GRS does not open a file in which a task has no finish.
Same as MSPDI Task/Milestone. Absent reads as false. When true, TaskVisual holds milestoneShape; otherwise it holds taskShape.
Same as MSPDI Task/Deadline.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualStart. Absent means the task is not started.
Same as MSPDI Task/Stop: the end of the actual work so far on a task that is in progress or suspended. On a finished task actualFinish holds that end; GRS empties stop when it finishes a task.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualFinish. Present only on a finished task; a percentComplete of 100 does not mean finished.
